title: When ...
subtitle: When I went out, it was raining.
summary: Join two parts into one sentence with when, before, while, after or until, and use the present after when for the future.

lesson.heading: Two parts in one sentence
lesson.text: A man opens his front door and sees rain everywhere, so he takes his umbrella. Later he tells a friend about it. He puts two parts together: **when I went out** + **it was raining**. Both orders are correct.

examples.text: **When I went out**, it was raining.
It was raining **when I went out**.

lesson.heading: When at the beginning or in the middle
lesson.text: You can put the **when**-part first or second. The meaning is the same. We write a comma (**,**) only when the **when**-part comes first.

lesson.heading: before / while / after
lesson.text: We do the same in sentences with **before**, **while** and **after**. The two parts can change places.

examples.text: Always look both ways **before** you cross the road.
**Before** you cross the road, always look both ways.
**While** I was waiting for the bus, it began to rain.
He never played football again **after** he broke his leg.

lesson.heading: When I am ... / When I go ...
lesson.text: Next week Sarah is going to New York. Her friend Lisa lives there, but Lisa is going away to Mexico. On the phone Lisa says: 'I'll be in Mexico **when you're** here.' The time is future, but after **when** we use the present.

examples.text: Lisa **will be** in Mexico **when** Sarah **is** in New York.
**When** I **get** home this evening, I'm going to have a shower.
I can't talk to you now. I'll talk to you later **when** I **have** more time.

lesson.heading: before / while / after / until + present
lesson.text: We do the same after **before**, **while**, **after** and **until**. The other part of the sentence often has *will* or *going to*.

examples.text: Please close the window **before** you **go** out.
Rachel is going to stay in our flat **while** we **are** away.

lesson.heading: We say / we do not say
rows: When I get home, I'm going to have a shower.
I'll talk to you when I have more time.
Close the window before you go out.
I'll wait here until you come back.

lesson.text: After when, before, while, after and until we use the present for the future: *I'll phone you when I get home*, not ~~when I will get home~~.

exercises.prompt: When I ___ home this evening, I'm going to have a shower.
exercises.explanation: After when we use the present, not will.

exercises.prompt: I'm going to bed when ___ my work.
exercises.explanation: After when we use the present: when I finish.

exercises.prompt: Match each when-part with the rest of the sentence.

pairs.right: I always go to the same place

pairs.left: When I got to the hotel,

exercises.prompt: We must do something before ___ too late.
exercises.explanation: After before we use the present: before it's too late.

exercises.prompt: I can't talk to you now. I'll talk to you later when I ___ more time.
exercises.explanation: After when we use the present, not will have.

exercises.prompt: Don't go out yet. Wait until the rain ___.
exercises.explanation: After until we use the present: until the rain stops.

exercises.statement: When I got to the hotel, there were no rooms.
exercises.explanation: Correct. Both parts are past, and the comma is right because the when-part comes first.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in the right order.
exercises.answer: When I'm tired, I like to watch TV.
exercises.explanation: The when-part comes first, so we write a comma after it.

exercises.prompt: Match the two halves of each sentence.

pairs.right: they went to live in New Zealand

pairs.left: Their house was damaged in a storm
When I told them what happened,

exercises.prompt: Helen is going away soon. ___ very sad when she leaves.
exercises.explanation: The other part of the sentence uses will: I'll be very sad when she leaves.

exercises.prompt: I'm not ready yet. I'll tell you when ___ ready.
exercises.explanation: Will goes in the other part, not after when: I'll tell you when I'm ready.

exercises.statement: I'll give it to you before I will go.
exercises.explanation: I'll give it to you before I go. After before we use the present, not will.
